content: The effects of desiccated thyroid may be reduced through an unknown mechanism. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. The estrogen component in combined hormonal contraceptives (CHCs) can increase serum concentrations of thyroxine-binding globulin, potentially necessitating higher doses of thyroid hormone replacement therapy in women using CHCs. Tigecycline can reduce the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended, as antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate can increase the levels or effects of tizanidine by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Combined oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol (EE) may inhibit the metabolism of cyclosporine, leading to increased plasma concentrations. Monitoring is recommended. Topiramate can decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be adjusted, and patients monitored closely. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, and alternative or backup contraception is recommended during use of enzyme inducers and for 28 days after discontinuation. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate can increase the levels or effects of triazolam by reducing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations of co-administered benzodiazepines. Monitoring is recommended. Trimethoprim can reduce the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended, as antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate and valoctocogene roxaparvovec may both increase the risk of elevated liver enzymes when combined with hepatotoxic medications. Close monitoring is required, and alternative medications should be considered in cases of potential drug interactions. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate can increase the levels or effects of voriconazole by reducing its metabolism. Voriconazole can also increase the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma hormone concentrations, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate can increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of enasidenib may increase or decrease the concentrations of combined hormonal contraceptives, though the clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. Levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate can decrease the levels or effects of acetaminophen through an unknown mechanism. Conversely, acetaminophen can increase the levels of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by reducing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration of ascorbic acid with certain CHCs containing EE may increase plasma EE concentrations, possibly by inhibiting conjugation. Monitoring is recommended. Oral contraceptives containing EE should be administered at least four hours before colesevelam to avoid significant reductions in EE levels. Atazanavir can cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. Similarly, belzutifan can reduce the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Nonhormonal contraception is advised, as belzutifan may also cause fetal harm. Bosentan, brigatinib, and butabarbital can reduce the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing contraceptive efficacy. Alternative or backup contraception is recommended during use and for 28 days after discontinuation. Brigatinib may also cause fetal harm, necessitating nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for four months after the last dose. Carbamazepine, cenobamate, and other CYP3A4 inducers can reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Women should use additional or alternative nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for 28 days after discontinuation. Cenobamate specifically requires close monitoring and alternative contraception due to its effects on oral contraceptive metabolism. Antibiotics such as cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime may reduce the levels or effects of oral levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. These interactions carry a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. Dexamethasone, efavirenz, and elafibranor can reduce the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for 28 days after discontinuation. Elafibranor may also require barrier methods or alternative contraception for at least three weeks after the last dose. Elagolix may have reduced efficacy when used with estrogen-containing contraceptives due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. Encorafenib can reduce the levels or effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing contraceptive failure. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. Encorafenib may also cause fetal harm. Enzalutamide, erythromycin, and other CYP3A4 inducers or antibiotics may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for 28 days after discontinuation.
